name: The Affray
summary: On Fray Island, warriors face a trial before Klannoc Macleod will train them. The Affray pits them against island challengers and their champion.

sections.title: A Proving Ground in the Great Sea
sections.body: Fray Island lies apart from the mainland, drawing brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not teach every wanderer who arrives by boat. Aspiring warriors must first enter the Affray, where stamina and awareness in battle prove who can fight beyond mere boasting.

sections.title: The Circle of Iron and Blood
sections.body: A warrior begins the Affray by stepping onto the central iron grate among the spectators. Ringmaster Twiggy Flathead then sends challengers into the ring one after another. Those who survive face the island's heavyweight champion, Big Will. Defeating him is the only way to earn Klannoc's respect.

faq.answer: The Affray tests aspiring warriors in a series of arena fights on Fray Island. Klannoc Macleod uses it to judge whether they are ready for advanced combat training.

faq.q: Where does the Affray take place?
faq.answer: The Affray takes place on Fray Island, off the eastern coast of the Barrens in the Great Sea.
Warrior trainer Klannoc Macleod oversees the island's fighters and sets the trial. Twiggy Flathead directs the bouts from the edge of the pit.

faq.q: How does the combat in the ring work?
faq.answer: A warrior steps onto the central iron grate to signal readiness. Twiggy Flathead sends Affray Challengers into the pit in waves, then releases the island champion, Big Will.
Big Will is the reigning champion of Fray Island's brawlers. Defeating him is the final requirement to pass the Affray.

faq.q: Why must warriors complete this trial?
faq.answer: Klannoc Macleod will not teach his martial techniques until a warrior proves their toughness in combat against multiple opponents.

angles.text: As a warrior, you face the Affray as a trial of your battle stances and endurance. Proving yourself there opens the way to deeper mastery of your craft.
